reviews.title: Fantastic airflow and build quality — shines when properly tuned
reviews.comment: I picked up the ARCTIC P14 Pro PST specifically for case airflow in a noise-sensitive build, and overall it’s an excellent fan — with one important caveat: it really rewards proper fan curve tuning. At low RPM, this fan is outstanding. Once dialed in, it moves a surprising amount of air while remaining very quiet, making it an excellent case fan for anyone prioritizing airflow without constant noise. You do need to put some effort into setting custom PWM curves to keep it in this sweet spot. Letting it ramp aggressively into the higher RPM range results in a noticeable jump in noise. At full speed, it gets quite loud — but it also pushes an impressive amount of air. Raw airflow performance is clearly a major strength here. Build quality is top-tier for the price. The frame feels rigid, the blades are well balanced, and overall it looks and feels more like a premium fan than a budget one. I didn’t notice any mechanical buzzing or wobble, even during RPM changes, and vibration was well controlled in my setup. One mounting note worth sharing: if you install this fan with the blades facing directly toward a restrictive surface (mesh panel, dust filter, radiator fins, etc.), the blade design can create odd harmonic noise when positioned too close. Using fan spacers or standoffs to add a bit of distance completely resolved this for me. With even a small gap to smooth airflow entry, the harmonics disappeared and the fan behaved normally again. PST daisy-chaining is a nice quality-of-life feature for cleaner cable management and unified PWM control. Pros: Exceptional airflow for a 140mm fan Excellent low-RPM noise profile when properly tuned Outstanding build quality PST daisy-chain PWM convenience Cons: Requires custom fan curves to fully benefit from quiet operation Gets loud at higher RPM May produce harmonics when mounted too close to restrictive surfaces without spacers Bottom line: The P14 Pro PST is an outstanding case fan if you’re willing to tune it properly. Keep it in the low-RPM range and give it adequate intake clearance, and you get excellent airflow at low noise with build quality that punches well above its price class. For high-RPM “blast air at all costs” use, it’s powerful but noisy — exactly what you’d expect from a fan optimized for airflow.
reviews.author: Martin

reviews.title: Awesome fans!
reviews.comment: I purchased these fans to replace these weak Coolermaster fans on my 280mm AIO in my Coolermaster NR200P Max case. With these new fans, I have seen a significant drop in CPU temps which has caused my system to become far more stable. My CPU would run at over 80 degrees with the CM fans while gaming and my PC would eventually freeze forcing me to do a forced reboot (holding power button). These Arctic fans have a higher CFM and static pressure to push the air through the 280mm radiator and mesh top cover causing my CPU temps to almost never exceed 75 degrees (except for some short spikes to the low-mid 80's). Even my CPU idle temps went from being around 50 to 53 degrees to being in the mid 40's even when my room is 27 degrees. And because if the better cooling, my CPU can boost higher and hold its boost speed longer. In terms of noise, these fans are a bit loud at speeds over 60% but that doesn't bother me too much. The fans are practically silent when the system is idling though. *All temps mentioned are in Celsius.
reviews.author: Matthew T.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment: These are the upgraded pwm fans. The 2500 rpm is insane, they def have the same noise profile and better pressure. Absolutely killer for the price. They have rubber seals that fit really well and don't extend past the normal range. Standard fan installation and the daisy chain cables are fantastic, they don't have harmonic resonance issues and perform better than the last models. 10/10 these are my go to if you want blacked out fans
reviews.author: Hammer

reviews.title: Good for builders on a budget.
reviews.comment: Good for builders on a budget. I like them they do their job and everyone is right they move a crapton of air. But do note that these are LOUD out of the box produce a sound similar to that of an angry mob of wasps but after some tuning they can be adjusted to be quieter and lower rpms. If you want a quiet machine i do not recommend these. But if you have a hot machine or are running high performance parts that typically run hot like any of the newer amd/intel chips and want to keep your temps down on a budget i can tell you these will probably get the job done at the cost or being louder than the more expensive competition. Another con is that the screws are hard to put in and I am an average adult man whos had experience building pcs before so i can tell you that compared to other fans, this assembly wasnt as easy as other, I rven ended up bending my case a bit trying to screw them in
reviews.author: Brandon

reviews.title: Ignore the haters! Calibrate these fans! They work perfectly!
reviews.comment: Ignore the people that are hating these fans because they are loud. They are loud because they can spin VERY fast and can push a lot of air. Make sure to calibrate these new fan in BIOS and then reduce their max speed to, for example, 60% if you want good airflow while keeping them dead quiet. They have absolutely ZERO motor noises. They are very high quality. I COULD NOT BE MORE HAPPY WITH THESE FANS!! Highly recommend!
